Technical details:
### Bug Summary The v1.6.3 tag references an otherwise-dangling commit that points to out of date revisions of submodules ### Detailed Description The v1.6.3 tag points to a dangling commit that has the wrong version of the USB library submodules, which means that users who clone and checkout the v1.6.3 tag of this repository will get an incorrect snapshot of the STM32Cube SDK. % git log --oneline --decorate --graph origin/master v1.6.3 -5 * c7446f41 (origin/master, origin/HEAD, master) [HAL] Upload new fixes * 878a6fd8 (HEAD) Release v1.6.3 | * bb9ba2a8 (tag: v1.6.3) Release v1.6.3 |/ * c80de4e0 [HAL] Upload new fixes * 24d13255 [HAL] Upload new fixes % git diff bb9ba2a8..878a6fd8 diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX index 70a56f3d..f61249a4 160000 --- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX +++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX @@ -1 +1 @@ -Subproject commit 70a56f3dda1827421a443e7e5e248807293c83cc +Subproject commit f61249a45ee3903075d2a94ce8c7c9c0c49e029d diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library index 555ce2b1..7b5e6886 160000 --- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library +++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library @@ -1 +1 @@ -Subproject commit 555ce2b1f7960031f153c93ed4e1c0bb95f34c95 +Subproject commit 7b5e6886d2f11ad15d2b46364e8a96984358f639 diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library index 38bc365e..9d46e44c 160000 --- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library +++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library @@ -1 +1 @@ -Subproject commit 38bc365e09b89c43b495af7261e31fe90a07335c +Subproject commit 9d46e44c858a77bf126920b7bcc258d59afa89b1 Note how commit bb9ba2a8 is what's tagged as v1.6.3, but commit 878a6fd8 "Release v1.6.3" is the commit actually reachable from the master branch. The difference is in revisions of USB library submodules, and it looks like the tagged commit bb9ba2a8 is the incorrect one. Based on commit author and tag timestamps, it looks like your release engineer amended the "Release v1.6.3" commit after they already created the v1.6.3 tag, and forgot to re-create the tag on the new fixed commit before pushing to GitHub. * STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX - Commit 70a56f3 is version 3.5.0 and commit f61249a is version 3.5.2 * STM32_USB_Device_Library - Commit 555ce2b is version 2.11.0 and commit 7b5e688 is 2.11.2 * STM32_USB_Host_Library - Commit 38bc365 is version 3.5.1 and commit 9d46e44 is 3.5.3 I compared this against the contents of ~/STM32Cube/Repository/STM32Cube_FW_G0_V1.6.3/Middlewares/ST/ that STM32CubeMX manages and can it looks like the official 1.6.3 release should have these newer USB library versions. ## How can this be resolved? Either update and force-push the v1.6.3 tag to point to 878a6fd8ad440c70ee32bc6d7ad526babb6e04f4, or make a new v1.6.4 release. ### Expected Behavior _No response_ ### Actual Behavior _No response_ ### Environment _No response_ ### Severity None

Key comments:
Hi @aswild, Good catch. Thank you for having reported. We'll try to have this fixed soon enough, hopefully. Hello @aswild, We have corrected the v1.6.3 tag so it now points to the intended release commit with the proper USB submodules revisions. Please update your local repository to get the corrected release snapshot Thank you again. Thanks @ALABSTM and @KRASTM! For reference to anyone else finding this issue, to update the tag in an existing clone you need to run git fetch --tags -f to force git to overwrite the local tag with the updated version from the server.

Problem: [Bug]: [STM32CubeMX LL] "Single Sample" (ONEBIT/CR3.ONEBIT) setting has no effect — not generated for LL driver
Context: repo=STM32CubeG0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=60
Root cause: Hello @eos1d3, Thank you for the report.
Fix: ### Bug Summary The "Single Sample" configuration option in CubeMX IOC has no effect when using LL drivers.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, low, bug, cube mx, lpuart, IOC, LL_USART_InitTypeDef, USART, ONEBIT, USART_CR3

Technical details:
### Bug Summary The "Single Sample" configuration option in CubeMX IOC has no effect when using LL drivers. No code is generated regardless of the setting, because LL_USART_InitTypeDef has no corresponding field. ### Detailed Description CubeMX exposes a "Single Sample" option for USART/LPUART configuration which maps to the ONEBIT bit in USART_CR3. This switches the receiver from a 3-sample majority vote to 1-sample per bit. When using HAL drivers, this setting correctly maps to UART_InitTypeDef.OneBitSampling and is generated into huart.Init.OneBitSampling = .... When using LL drivers, LL_USART_InitTypeDef has no OneBitSampling or equivalent field. As a result: - CubeMX generates no code for this setting regardless of the IOC value - There is no warning or error indicating the setting was ignored - The behavior is the same whether "Enable" or "Disable" is selected This affects USART1, USART2, and LPUART1. MCU/MPU Series: STM32G031 (likely all STM32 series with LL driver support) Firmware Package: STM32Cube FW_G0 IDE: STM32CubeIDE Driver type: LL ### Expected Behavior LL_USART_InitTypeDef should include an OneBitSampling field and generate LL_USART_EnableOneSampling() / LL_USART_DisableOneSampling() accordingly, or CubeMX should display a warning that this setting is not supported for LL drivers and will be ignored. ### Actual Behavior The setting is silently ignored. No code is generated and no warning is shown, leaving the developer unaware that their configuration has no effect. The hardware always uses the reset default (3-sample mode) regardless of the IOC setting. ### Environment STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319) ### Severity None

Hello @eos1d3, Thank you for the report. Could you please share the version of CubeMx you are using and if possible, your IOC file? It does exist in HAL. Hello @eos1d3, After checking the documentation and referring to **RM0444 Rev 6**, the **ONEBIT / Single Sample** feature is not available for LPUART. Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, UART, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, cube mx, lpuart, LPUART1, DMA-, RX-, DDRE

Technical details:
### Bug Summary CubeMX LL code generator produces inverted function calls for LPUART1 overrun detection and DMA-deactivation-on-RX-error (DDRE). Selecting "Disabled" in the IOC generates Enable*() calls. ### Detailed Description In the CubeMX IOC configuration for LPUART1, the "Overrun detection" and "DMA on RX error" settings produce inverted LL function calls in the generated MX_LPUART1_UART_Init(): - Setting Disabled in IOC → generates [LL_LPUART_EnableOverrunDetect(LPUART1)](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) and [LL_LPUART_EnableDMADeactOnRxErr(LPUART1)](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) - Setting Enabled in IOC → generates no function calls at all The same settings on USART1 and USART2 generate correct polarity (DisableOverrunDetect when Disabled is selected). MCU/MPU Series: STM32G031 Firmware Package: STM32Cube FW_G0 IDE: STM32CubeIDE Driver type: LL ### Expected Behavior Selecting Disabled should generate LL_LPUART_DisableOverrunDetect() / LL_LPUART_DisableDMADeactOnRxErr() Selecting Enabled should generate LL_LPUART_EnableOverrunDetect() / LL_LPUART_EnableDMADeactOnRxErr() (or no call, since enabled is the reset default) ### Actual Behavior Polarity is inverted for LPUART1 only — Disabled generates Enable calls. The hardware reset default for both settings is enabled, so with "Enabled" in the IOC generating no code, the actual hardware state happens to be correct by accident. However, selecting "Disabled" silently enables overrun detection instead of disabling it. ### Environment STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319) ### Severity None

Problem: STM32G0 HAL UART IRQ Handler Missing IDLE Event Handling in DMA Circular Mode
Context: repo=STM32CubeG0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=DMA, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=57
Root cause: Hello @SONGMENGSEN, Thank you for the report.
Fix: ## Issue Description ### Problem Summary There is a functional inconsistency between the STM32G0 and STM32H7 series HAL libraries in the [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, DMA, bug_report, medium, bug, uart, STM32G0, STM32H7, HAL_UART_IRQHandler, flux_temp, temp_10_20_485, IDLE

Technical details:
## Issue Description ### Problem Summary There is a functional inconsistency between the STM32G0 and STM32H7 series HAL libraries in the [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) implementation. Specifically, the STM32G0 version lacks the logic to handle IDLE events in DMA circular mode, which can lead to improper event notification to the application layer under certain usage scenarios. ### Detailed Description 1. **Inconsistent DMA Circular Mode Checking Approach**: - STM32G0 uses [HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(huart->hdmarx->Instance->CCR, DMA_CCR_CIRC)](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Openlib\perf_counter\CI\perf_counter_template_gcc\Drivers\STM32F1xx_HAL_Driver\Inc\stm32f1xx_hal_def.h#L59-L60) - STM32H7 uses huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode != DMA_CIRCULAR 2. **Missing IDLE Event Handling in Circular Mode**: The STM32H7 version includes the following logic in [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) that is missing in the STM32G0 version: c /* If DMA is in Circular mode, Idle event is to be reported to user even if occurring after a Transfer Complete event from DMA */ if (nb_remaining_rx_data == huart->RxXferSize) { if (huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode == DMA_CIRCULAR) { /* Initialize type of RxEvent that correspond to RxEvent callback execution; In this case, Rx Event type is Idle Event */ huart->RxEventType = HAL_UART_RXEVENT_IDLE; // Callback invocation } } ### Impact When using DMA circular mode for UART reception, if an IDLE line event occurs after the reception buffer is filled, the STM32G0 version will not notify the application layer. This may result in delayed data processing or missed event notifications. ### Expected Fix It is recommended to unify the [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) implementation between STM32G0 and STM32H7 series, enhancing the STM32G0 version's functional completeness to ensure consistent behavior across all usage scenarios. This would involve: 1. Standardizing the DMA circular mode detection method 2. Adding the missing IDLE event handling logic for circular mode operation ### Environment - MCU Series: STM32G0 - HAL Library Version: [Please specify version] - Affected Module: UART HAL driver ([stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c)) - Function: [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627)

Key comments:
Hello @SONGMENGSEN, Thank you for the report. Regarding your request about the implementation of HAL_UART_IRQHandler() API, there is no difference between the 2 solutions and neither impacts functionality or behavior—unless you have a specific use case in your project. For your reference, an enhancement was added to notify users of the HAL_UART_RXEVENT_IDLE event in this commit https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/commit/d9c6bb8de5cb483c8a2d896ffd5e2796f60bccf4. Additionally, I tested the example located at STM32CubeG0\Projects\STM32G0C1E-EV\Examples\UART\UART_ReceptionToIdle_CircularDMA and works as expected, you can check it for more details. If you have any further information to share, kindly let us know. Otherwise, I will proceed to close this thread. Thank you for your understanding. Add HAL_UART_RXEVENT_IDLE event notification to user in case of HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() use with Circular DMA, even if occurring just after TC event This is exactly the problem I encountered. Since it has been solved, I just need to update it , Thank you

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: PREFETCH_ENABLE not implemented
Context: repo=STM32CubeG0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=56
Root cause: In: STM32Cube_FW_G0\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal.
Fix: In STM32G0xx_hal_conf.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, flash, VDD_VALUE, VDD, TICK_INT_PRIORITY, USE_RTOS, PREFETCH_ENABLE, INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE

Technical details:
In STM32G0xx_hal_conf.h, these macros are defined: #define VDD_VALUE (3300UL) /*!< Value of VDD in mv */ #define TICK_INT_PRIORITY 0U /*!< tick interrupt priority */ #define USE_RTOS 0U #define PREFETCH_ENABLE 0U #define INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE 1U As far as I can tell, PREFETCH_ENABLE is not implemented and has no affect on any of the library code. In order to disable prefetch we had to add the following in our main.c after SystemClock_Config(): // CRITICAL: Explicitly disable prefetch for STM32G0 errata 2.2.10 // The PREFETCH_ENABLE define in hal_conf.h is NOT used by the HAL // We must manually clear the PRFTEN bit in FLASH->ACR // Confirm that prefetch is not disabled by setting PREFETCH_ENABLE to 0 if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN) != 0) { CLEAR_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN); } // Verify prefetch is actually disabled if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN) != 0) { // Prefetch failed to disable - this should never happen Error_Handler(); } As noted in my comment above, this directly addresses the "silicon bug" described in errata 2.2.10, as anyone attempting to disable prefetch in the CubeMX/IDE GUI may not realize that doing this in the gui (or the header) has no effect. We fought random hardfaults for 2 months to no avail until we discovered this bug, and lost an hour or so not realizing that we had to manually disable prefetch with the above code. For what it's worth, I'm not sure INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE is implemented either.

Key comments:
In: STM32Cube_FW_G0\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal.c HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_Init(void) #if (PREFETCH_ENABLE != 0U) __HAL_FLASH_PREFETCH_BUFFER_ENABLE(); #endif /* PREFETCH_ENABLE */ [IMAGE ATTACHED] [IMAGE ATTACHED] So Prefetch enable shouldn't need an explicit disable if RM0444 Rev 6 is correct on reset behavior. To be clear, are you seeing prefetch enable bit set after reset? Are you writing to FLASH->ACR elsewhere in the code? We ran into this erata before it was published, was a bit of a nightmare. fixing PREFETCH_ENABLE setting did work for us tho Hello @insolace, As mentioned by @DanLiemanGalvion, the **PRFTEN** bit is cleared at initial state. After investigation and analyzing, I did not find any manipulation of this bit within our HAL code except at the following lines in HAL_Init function: #if (PREFETCH_ENABLE != 0U) __HAL_FLASH_PREFETCH_BUFFER_ENABLE(); #endif /* PREFETCH_ENABLE */ Therefore, it is impossible to set the **PRFTEN** bit if PREFETCH_ENABLE = 0U. From my side our example is functioning correctly and there is no manipulation of **PRFTEN** bit only when PREFETCH_ENABLE = 1U. @DanLiemanGalvion thank you for your intervention. B

hdma_usart5_tx.Init.Mode = DMA_NORMAL; hdma_usart5_tx.Init.Priority = DMA_PRIORITY_LOW; HAL_DMA_Init(&hdma_usart5_tx); // Link DMA handle with USART5 handle __HAL_LINKDMA(&usart5, hdmatx, hdma_usart5_tx); usart5.Init.BaudRate = SERIAL_UART_BAUD_RATE; usart5.Init.WordLength = UART_WORDLENGTH_8B; usart5.Init.StopBits = UART_STOPBITS_1; usart5.Init.Parity = UART_PARITY_NONE; usart5.Init.Mode = UART_MODE_TX_RX; usart5.Init.HwFlowCtl = UART_HWCONTROL_NONE; usart5.Init.OverSampling = UART_OVERSAMPLING_16; usart5.Init.OneBitSampling = UART_ONE_BIT_SAMPLE_DISABLE; usart5.AdvancedInit.AdvFeatureInit = UART_ADVFEATURE_NO_INIT; if (HAL_UART_Init(&usart5) != HAL_OK) { while(1); // Need to switch out while(1) for proper error handling } // Enable UART interrupts HAL_NVIC_SetPriority(USART3_4_5_6_IRQn, USART3_4_5_6_IRQ_PREEMPT_PRIORITY, USART3_4_5_6_IRQ_SUB_PRIORITY); HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ(USART3_4_5_6_IRQn); Here is the #define that fails: #define IS_DMA_ALL_REQUEST(REQUEST) ((REQUEST) <= DMA_MAX_REQUEST) where: DMA_MAX_REQUEST is defined as: #define DMA_MAX_REQUEST LL_DMAMUX_MAX_REQ and In stm32g0xx_ll_dmamux.h #elif defined(STM32G0B0xx) #define LL_DMAMUX_MAX_REQ LL_DMAMUX_REQ_USART4_TX **Additional context** Since there are the peripherals USART5 and USART6 that can use DMA on this platform, the proper define should be: #define LL_DMAMUX_MAX_REQ LL_DMAMUX_REQ_USART6_TX **Screenshots** [IMAGE ATTACHED]

Problem: not usefull const in stm32g0xx_ll_dma.h
Context: repo=STM32CubeG0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=DMA, layer=LL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=51
Root cause: Similare in stm32g0xx_ll_dmamux.
Fix: const is one of the importers keywords in C/C++.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: LL, DMA, bug_report, medium, enhancement, invalid, internal bug tracker, hal, LL_DMA_EnableChannel, DMA_TypeDef, dma_base_addr, SET_BIT

Technical details:
const is one of the importers keywords in C/C++. It is great, that you add more and more const. Const tell the compiler, that the symbol is not writable. For example, Get function should set const for the object Set function should not set const for the object But now you add const to object that are modified. For example, __STATIC_INLINE void LL_DMA_EnableChannel(const DMA_TypeDef *DMAx, uint32_t Channel) { uint32_t dma_base_addr = (uint32_t)DMAx; SET_BIT(((DMA_Channel_TypeDef *)(dma_base_addr + CHANNEL_OFFSET_TAB[Channel]))->CCR, DMA_CCR_EN); } This function modifies *DMAx. So DMAx should not be const. Here it works because you cast DMAx to a uint32_t and so you lost the const attribute. Casting is always a dangerous modification! Please remove const from DMA_TypeDef *DMAx in the following functions LL_DMA_EnableChannel() LL_DMA_DisableChannel() LL_DMA_ConfigTransfer() LL_DMA_SetDataTransferDirection() LL_DMA_SetMode() LL_DMA_SetPeriphIncMode() LL_DMA_SetMemoryIncMode() LL_DMA_SetMemoryIncMode() LL_DMA_SetMemorySize() LL_DMA_SetChannelPriorityLevel() LL_DMA_SetDataLength() LL_DMA_ConfigAddresses() LL_DMA_SetMemoryAddress() LL_DMA_SetPeriphAddress() LL_DMA_SetM2MSrcAddress() LL_DMA_SetM2MDstAddress() LL_DMA_SetPeriphRequest () LL_DMA_EnableIT_TC () LL_DMA_EnableIT_HT() BTW. It is best practice when the pointer to an object is const. For example, DMA_TypeDef *DMAx Should be replaced with DMA_TypeDef * const DMAx So the object can modified but the pointer can’t be modified.

Key comments:
Similare in stm32g0xx_ll_dmamux.h ST Internal Reference: 186542 Hello @RetoFx, In both stm32g0xx_ll_dma.h stm32g0xx_ll_dmamux.h: In all these functions, DMAx is not modified. The conversion (uint32_t)DMAx is used to obtain a numerical representation of the base address of the DMA peripheral, which allows calculating the address of the specific DMA_Channel. This address is then used to access and modify the CCR, CPAR, CMAR, or CNDTR register of the DMA_Channel that already exists in the DMA_Channel_TypeDef structure. typedef struct { __IO uint32_t CCR; /*!< DMA channel x configuration register */ __IO uint32_t CNDTR; /*!< DMA channel x number of data register */ __IO uint32_t CPAR; /*!< DMA channel x peripheral address register */ __IO uint32_t CMAR; /*!< DMA channel x memory address register */ } DMA_Channel_TypeDef; Therefore, in this case, the pointer DMAx is read-only (const).

When I perform the following sequence the first time, everything works: Slave -> HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT Master -> HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit_IT Slave -> HAL_I2C_SlaveRxCpltCallback -> HAL_I2C_Slave_Transmit_IT Master -> HAL_I2C_MasterTxCpltCallback -> HAL_I2C_Master_Receive_IT Slave -> HAL_I2C_SlaveTxCpltCallback -> HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT And repeat.... The issue is that hi2c->XferCount and hi2c->XferSize are both zero, but tmpoptions is set to I2C_NO_OPTION_FRAME so it never completes. Also, TXIS and TXE are set to 1, so the transfer thinks it's incomplete, and continues to run indefinitely, holding the clock line low. **Additional context** I have been unable to figure out the cause of this, but I've spent a LONG time looking in to it. It appears to be an issue with HAL.

Problem: I2C addr flag not reset inside I2C_ITAddrCplt
Context: repo=STM32CubeG0, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=31
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 149407 Hi @kjsdf7wr3, The addr flag is not cleared intentionally in the case of listen.
Fix: Inside I2C_ITAddrCplt the address flag is reset for - 10bit mode (if event count == 2) - listen is disabled it is **not reset** for - 7bit mode - 10bit mode (if event count == 1) See https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, invalid, question, internal bug tracker, HAL_I2C_AddrCallback, HAL_I2C_CLEAR_FLAG

Technical details:
Inside I2C_ITAddrCplt the address flag is reset for - 10bit mode (if event count == 2) - listen is disabled it is **not reset** for - 7bit mode - 10bit mode (if event count == 1) See https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/blob/03cb8e9ec0cbefad623caebe47359df0bab1d05e/Drivers/STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L5486 I think this is an error, it should be reset in all cases before calling HAL_I2C_AddrCallback(hi2c, transferdirection, slaveaddrcode);. This means HAL_I2C_CLEAR_FLAG(hi2c, I2C_FLAG_ADDR); should be added in the two cases mentioned above. If the flag is not reset, the chip will pull the clock line low forever after receiving its slave address.

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 149407 Hi @kjsdf7wr3, The addr flag is not cleared intentionally in the case of listen. Actually, this allows to force a stretch of the line until the application calls the slave sequential interfaces. The stretch makes possible to block the master, as long as the slave app has not prepared its use case via the sequential interfaces. Since this is not an issue, please allow me thus to close this thread.

Keywords: NUCLEO-G071RB, HAL, usage_question, medium, question, STM32, TIM2, CC2E, STM32G071, MX_TIM2_Init, HAL_TIM_Base_Start, HAL_OK

Technical details:
**Caution** The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project. For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus). **Describe the set-up** * NUCLEO-G071RB as well as a custom board with a G0B1KCT * CubeIDE 1.7.0, fw package 1.4.1 **Describe the bug** When TIM2 is configured as pwm input capture to capture both duty and frequency, and capturing is enabled, CC2E is not set resulting in failure to acquire the second register value. **How To Reproduce** 1. Configure TIM2 with CubeMX on a STM32G071 like in the picture, pay attention to the fact that Channel1 is on rising edge, while Channel2 is on falling edge ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54371771/139463058-35fc062d-cb91-4a3c-9454-36f4836c1118.png) 2. in the code, call everything necessary to start the capture MX_TIM2_Init(); if (HAL_TIM_Base_Start(&htim2) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } HAL_TIM_IC_Init(&htim2); HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_1); 3. CC2E won't be set, so only the rising edge interrupt will be generated 4. Solution is to add bit set operation after starting the capture /* Enable also the capture on the falling edge for Duty Cycle */ TIM2->CCER |= TIM_CCER_CC2E; Timer2 setup code as generated by CubeMX void MX_TIM2_Init(void) { /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM2_Init 0 */ /* USER CODE END TIM2_Init 0 */ TIM_ClockConfigTypeDef sClockSourceConfig = {0}; TIM_SlaveConfigTypeDef sSlaveConfig = {0}; TIM_MasterConfigTypeDef sMasterConfig = {0}; TIM_IC_InitTypeDef sConfigIC = {0}; /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM2_Init 1 */ /* USER CODE END TIM2_Init 1 */ htim2.Instance = TIM2; htim2.Init.Prescaler = 100 - 1; htim2.Init.CounterMode = TIM_COUNTERMODE_UP; htim2.Init.Period = 0xFFFFFFFF; htim2.Init.ClockDivision = TIM_CLOCKDIVISION_DIV1; htim2.Init.AutoReloadPreload = TIM_AUTORELOAD_PRELOAD_DISABLE; if (HAL_TIM_Base_Init(&htim2) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } sClockSourceConfig.ClockSource = TIM_CLOCKSOURCE_INTERNAL; if (HAL_TIM_ConfigClockSource(&htim2, &sClockSourceConfig) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } if (HAL_TIM_IC_Init(&htim2) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } sSlaveConfig.SlaveMode = TIM_SLAVEMODE_RESET; sSlaveConfig.InputTrigger = TIM_TS_TI1FP1; sSlaveConfig.TriggerPolarity = TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_RISING; sSlaveConfig.TriggerFilter = 0; if (HAL_TIM_SlaveConfigSynchro(&htim2, &sSlaveConfig) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } sMasterConfig.MasterOutputTrigger = TIM_TRGO_RESET; sMasterConfig.MasterSlaveMode = TIM_MASTERSLAVEMODE_DISABLE; if (HAL_TIMEx_MasterConfigSynchronization(&htim2, &sMasterConfig) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } sConfigIC.ICPolarity = TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_RISING; sConfigIC.ICSelection = TIM_ICSELECTION_DIRECTTI; sConfigIC.ICPrescaler = TIM_ICPSC_DIV1; sConfigIC.ICFilter = 0; if (HAL_TIM_IC_ConfigChannel(&htim2, &sConfigIC, TIM_CHANNEL_1) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } sConfigIC.ICPolarity = TIM_INPUTCHANNELPOLARITY_FALLING; sConfigIC.ICSelection = TIM_ICSELECTION_INDIRECTTI; if (HAL_TIM_IC_ConfigChannel(&htim2, &sConfigIC, TIM_CHANNEL_2) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM2_Init 2 */ /* USER CODE END TIM2_Init 2 */ }

Key comments:
Hi @embcla, An instruction is missing in your code so that you can activate the CC2E. The code should then be: diff MX_TIM2_Init(); if (HAL_TIM_Base_Start(&htim2) != HAL_OK) { Error_Handler(); } HAL_TIM_IC_Init(&htim2); HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_1); + HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_2); The HAL_TIM_IC_Start_IT(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_2) function will starts the TIM Input Capture measurement in interrupt mode on the channel 2 and enables the TIM Capture Compare on the specified channel. I hope this would help you. Hello @ASELSTM and thank you for taking a look at this. The confusion comes from the fact that I couldn't find this mentioned anywhere. The STM32G0x1 RM0444 manual only mentions specific bits and registers, while the HAL has no example usage of groups of functions. Bridging that gap proved hard for me. The spec says that the sender must give up the line within 23uS (tEndDriveBMC) after the end of the frame. The STMicro library, at least when used with a bare-metal codebase, seems to check the bus at around 10uS.. and only checks it once. If the bus is busy, it just throws the packet away. This is catastrophic since this can happen when trying to send a GoodCRC message. **How To Reproduce** 1. Find port partner source who gives up the bus close to tEndDriveBMC time. The https://www.st.com/en/evaluation-tools/p-nucleo-usb002.html is about 17uS and is a good candidate. 2. Configure the STM32G0 as a SNK. 3. Using a PD sniffer, observe lack of GoodCRCs **Additional context** This patch below keeps me moving forward. However, I think a better solution is to place a **23uS** delay after message received to guarantee that the firmware won't check the CC bus too early. --- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_hw_if_it.c +++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_hw_if_it.c @@ -51,6 +51,7 @@ void PORTx_IRQHandler(uint8_t PortNum) UCPD_TypeDef *hucpd = Ports[PortNum].husbpd; uint32_t _interrupt = LL_UCPD_ReadReg(hucpd, SR); static uint8_t ovrflag = 0; + static uint8_t tx_retry = 0;^M if ((hucpd->IMR & _interrupt) != 0u) { @@ -59,7 +60,14 @@ void PORTx_IRQHandler(uint8_t PortNum) { /* the message has been discarded */ LL_UCPD_ClearFlag_TxMSGDISC(hucpd); - CLEAR_BIT(Ports[PortNum].hdmatx->CCR, DMA_CCR_EN); + if(tx_retry != 2) { + tx_retry++; + LL_UCPD_SendMessage(Ports[PortNum].husbpd); + } + else { + tx_retry = 0; + CLEAR_BIT(Ports[PortNum].hdmatx->CCR, DMA_CCR_EN); + } return; }
